touches.text: A request seen before is answered from the stored answer, if it still holds, and the host is not touched. That untouched call is compilation.

The stored answers are learning, so they live in the memory model: a tree the proxy holds by the librarian's delegation, asking "what did this request answer?". An answer is found by its exact request and carries no embedding (4.3.1.6). The meter (every call, its verdict and cost) is not learning: it is metrics (17.27). The inference ticket, a file in the logs tree on the 30 day clock, is only for debugging.

Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged. [Q#90: A proof's seal is one record, so the newest OS to seal replaces the other's, and a proof with teeth for both OSes reds on every single OS. Measured 2026-11-12: a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal. Do seals go per OS (validations/<os>/, or an OS key in the record), or is one OS the sealing box?]

A row number is the same on every box. Storing a memory first reserves its slot from the librarian on the home box (CAIRN_HOME_HOST, 6.3.7.4), so two boxes are never handed the same slot, and the slot stays reserved until the write is complete. If a box's list is shorter than the slot (eg it holds rows up to 100 and is handed 123 while a sync is bringing the rest), it adds the open slots in between as blanks, and the sync fills them in as it proceeds. WHY: node ids are in every link and blob pointer, so a row has to mean the same node everywhere.

A remote box keeps its own database and syncs it with the home box's (6.3.7.4). Node rows are the same on every box; the sync fills the blanks a box holds open (4.3.1.5.1.1). WHY: the local copy is fast, and the sync is the backup.

metric: records a measurement of anything. WHY: a metric is a primitive; its job is to measure whatever it is, and like feedback (which a metric strictly is) it must eventually have a consumer. USERS: any probe or tool.
Transient: things held for seconds to days (mail, logs, test runs, trouble tickets, inference tickets). The logging tree.

conflicts.why: Outline 11.4.4.1 explicitly states 'The meter (every call, its verdict and cost) is not learning: it is metrics (17.27)'. Outline 4.3.2 and 17.27 distinguish between the transient logging tree (4.3.2) and metrics—permanent records (17.27.5: 'Rows are kept forever'). If 'the log' refers to the transient logging tree (as the outline uses the term), meter cannot simultaneously be in both metrics (permanent, outline spec) and the log (transient, ticket statement).
